es.summary: La fibrosis pulmonar es una enfermedad crónica en la que el tejido intersticial de los pulmones se cicatriza, reduciendo la elasticidad y la capacidad de intercambio gaseoso.
key_points: Patrón respiratorio ineficaz por pérdida de compliance pulmonar.
Disnea progresiva y tos seca son los síntomas cardinales.
Diagnóstico mediante TC de alta resolución y pruebas de función pulmonar.
Complicaciones incluyen hipertensión pulmonar y cor pulmonale.

pathophysiology: Daño alveolar crónico → inflamación → depósito de colágeno.
Engrosamiento del intersticio disminuye la elasticidad pulmonar.
Reducción del volumen residual y capacidad vital forzada.
risk_factors: Exposición a polvo de sílice, asbesto o gases tóxicos.
Medicamentos como amiodarona, nitrofurantoína o quimioterapia.
Enfermedades del tejido conectivo (esclerodermia, artritis reumatoide).
signs_symptoms: Disnea de esfuerzo que progresa a reposo.
Fatiga y pérdida de peso involuntaria.
diagnostics: TC de alta resolución: patrón en vidrio esmerilado y bronquiectasias de tracción.
Espirometría: FVC < 80% predicho, relación FEV1/FVC normal o alta.
treatment: Rehabilitación pulmonar: ejercicios de respiración y entrenamiento aeróbico.
complications: Cor pulmonale y insuficiencia cardíaca derecha.
nursing_care: Evaluar frecuencia respiratoria, esfuerzo y uso de musculatura accesoria.
Monitorear SpO2 y PaO2; mantener SaO2 ≥ 92% con oxígeno.
Posicionar semi‑Fowler para mejorar expansión torácica.
Administrar antifibróticos según prescripción y observar hepatotoxicidad.
Educar sobre técnicas de drenaje postural y respiración diafragmática.
patient_teaching: Evitar exposición a contaminantes y humo de cigarro.
Adherir al tratamiento antifibrótico y reportar síntomas hepáticos.
Uso seguro del oxígeno domiciliario (no fumar, revisar conexiones).
Planificar actividades con descansos para conservar energía.

outcomes: Patrón respiratorio eficaz: SpO2 ≥ 92% en reposo
Disminución de la disnea: escala Borg ≤ 3 durante actividades de la vida diaria

interventions.action: Evaluar frecuencia respiratoria y auscultar campos pulmonares cada turno
interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios tempranos en la función respiratoria

interventions.action: Administrar oxígeno suplementario según orden médica, ajustando flujo para mantener SaO2 ≥ 92%
interventions.rationale: Previene hipoxemia y reduce el trabajo respiratorio

interventions.action: Enseñar respiración diafragmática y ejercicios de expansión torácica
interventions.rationale: Mejora la ventilación y disminuye la disnea

interventions.action: Posicionar al paciente en semi‑Fowler con soporte lumbar
interventions.rationale: Facilita la expansión pulmonar y reduce el esfuerzo respiratorio

interventions.action: Monitorear signos de toxicidad hepática al iniciar pirfenidona o nintedanib
interventions.rationale: Los antifibróticos pueden causar hepatotoxicidad

evidenced_by: reducción de la tolerancia al ejercicio
outcomes: Tolerancia a la actividad: caminar 150 metros sin disnea significativa
Nivel de energía: puntuación ≥ 5 en escala de energía de 0‑10

interventions.action: Planificar actividades en bloques de 10‑15 minutos con descansos programados
interventions.rationale: Conserva energía y evita la sobrecarga respiratoria

interventions.action: Implementar programa de rehabilitación pulmonar supervisado
interventions.rationale: Mejora la capacidad aeróbica y la resistencia muscular

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de conservación de energía (sentarse para tareas, usar ayudas de movilidad)
interventions.rationale: Reduce el gasto energético durante actividades diarias

interventions.action: Evaluar nutrición y peso; referir a dietista si hay pérdida de peso >5% en 6 meses
interventions.rationale: Mantener masa muscular es esencial para la tolerancia al ejercicio

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales antes y después de la actividad física
interventions.rationale: Detecta descompensación temprana y guía ajustes en el plan de ejercicio

en.summary: Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic disease in which the lung interstitium scars, reducing elasticity and gas exchange capacity.
key_points: Ineffective respiratory pattern due to loss of pulmonary compliance.
Progressive dyspnea and dry cough are cardinal symptoms.
Diagnosis via high‑resolution CT and pulmonary function tests.
Complications include pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

pathophysiology: Chronic alveolar injury → inflammation → collagen deposition.
Reduced residual volume and forced vital capacity.
risk_factors: Exposure to silica dust, asbestos, or toxic gases.
Medications such as amiodarone, nitrofurantoin, or chemotherapy.
diagnostics: High‑resolution CT: ground‑glass pattern and traction bronchiectasis.
Spirometry: FVC < 80% predicted, normal or high FEV1/FVC ratio.
Arterial blood gas: PaO2 < 80 mmHg, SaO2 < 92%.
treatment: Pulmonary rehabilitation: breathing exercises and aerobic training.
nursing_care: Assess respiratory rate, effort, and accessory muscle use.
Monitor SpO2 and PaO2; maintain SaO2 ≥ 92% with oxygen.
Position semi‑Fowler to improve thoracic expansion.
Administer antifibrotics per prescription and monitor hepatotoxicity.
Educate on postural drainage and diaphragmatic breathing techniques.
patient_teaching: Avoid exposure to pollutants and cigarette smoke.
Adhere to antifibrotic therapy and report hepatic symptoms.
Use home oxygen safely (no smoking, check connections).
Plan activities with rest breaks to conserve energy.
Get vaccinated against influenza and pneumococcus.

outcomes: Effective respiratory pattern: SpO2 ≥ 92% at rest
Reduced dyspnea: Borg scale ≤ 3 during activities of daily living

interventions.action: Assess respiratory rate and auscultate lung fields each shift
interventions.rationale: Detect early changes in respiratory function

interventions.action: Administer supplemental oxygen per order, adjusting flow to maintain SaO2 ≥ 92%
interventions.rationale: Prevents hypoxemia and reduces work of breathing

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and thoracic expansion exercises
interventions.rationale: Improves ventilation and decreases dyspnea

interventions.action: Position patient in semi‑Fowler with lumbar support
interventions.rationale: Facilitates lung expansion and reduces respiratory effort

interventions.action: Monitor hepatic toxicity signs when starting pirfenidone or nintedanib
interventions.rationale: Antifibrotics can cause hepatotoxicity

outcomes: Activity tolerance: walk 150 meters without significant dyspnea
Energy level: score ≥ 5 on 0‑10 energy scale

interventions.action: Schedule activities in 10‑15 minute blocks with planned rest
interventions.rationale: Conserves energy and avoids respiratory overload

interventions.action: Implement supervised pulmonary rehabilitation program
interventions.rationale: Improves aerobic capacity and muscular endurance

interventions.action: Teach energy conservation techniques (sit for tasks, use mobility aids)
interventions.rationale: Reduces energy expenditure during daily activities

interventions.action: Assess nutrition and weight; refer to dietitian if weight loss >5% in 6 months
interventions.rationale: Maintaining muscle mass is essential for exercise tolerance

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs before and after physical activity
interventions.rationale: Detects early decompensation and guides exercise plan adjustments

summary.0.quote: Interstitial lung disease is the name for a large group of diseases that inflame or scar the lungs.

key_points.1.quote: Symptoms include: Shortness of breath A dry, hacking cough that doesn't get better Fatigue Weight loss for no known reason Aching muscles and joints Clubbing, which is the widening and rounding of the tips of the fingers or toes

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Employment-related exposure may also include populations who mine granite or sandstone and are therefore exposed to silica dust, and coal miners, who are exposed to coal dust and at risk for pneumoconiosis (“black lung”).

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Symptoms include: Shortness of breath A dry, hacking cough that doesn't get better Fatigue Weight loss for no known reason Aching muscles and joints Clubbing, which is the widening and rounding of the tips of the fingers or toes Your doctor may use your medical history, imaging tests, a biopsy, and lung function tests to diagnose pulmonary fibrosis.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Symptoms include: Shortness of breath A dry, hacking cough that doesn't get better Fatigue Weight loss for no known reason Aching muscles and joints Clubbing, which is the widening and rounding of the tips of the fingers or toes Your doctor may use your medical history, imaging tests, a biopsy, and lung function tests to diagnose pulmonary fibrosis.

sections.complications.3.quote: Smoking causes a disruption of the mucociliary elevator in the lungs, which can lead to increased colonization of bacteria in the lower respiratory tract and frequent infections.
